segments.title: Meeting Brother Montgomery in the 1920s
segments.summary: The interviewer asks when and where Tuts met Little Brother Montgomery; it was back in the 1920s, near Second Street.

segments.title: Honky-tonk piano contests, Red Cayou, Tatum, Kid Clayton and Tillman bands
segments.summary: One long block: Tuts names the older and rival New Orleans pianists (Leon Mumfrey, Lester Lewis, Tink Baptiste, Red Cayou), how piano 'bucking' won him his name, the Celestin band, his idol Tatum, Stormy Weather, and his bands under Kid Clayton and Wilbur Tillman.

segments.title: Boogers and Joe Hopkins, who played only the black keys
segments.summary: Tuts describes Sammy Hopkins' brother, a pianist who played everything in F-sharp on the black keys and so never worked in bands.

segments.title: Poor Ray Nolan, Jimmy Cato and other pianists he knew
segments.summary: Asked about more pianists, Tuts recalls Poor Ray Nolan, Jimmy Cato and his cousin Adam Cato, and little Butch.

segments.title: Researcher asks Walter Lewis about Stormy Weather and the Tulane and Broad record
segments.summary: The interviewer explains how he traced Stormy Weather's Jackson, Mississippi records to New Orleans; Walter Lewis knows him only by nickname as a boogie-woogie blues player.

segments.title: Red Cayou and Fate Marable on the riverboat
segments.summary: Walter Lewis recalls that Red Cayou and Fate Marable worked on the steamer Capitol, and that it was mostly band work with some solos.

segments.title: Versatility of the old blues pianists and never finishing learning
segments.summary: Lewis says the old players were popular because they could play anything, not just one blues, and that a musician never stops learning.

segments.title: Possible kinship with Steve Lewis, Lewis's nap routine and a photograph
segments.summary: Talk about whether Lewis was related to Steve Lewis, names that change, his work hours and nap, and the researcher asking to take his picture.

segments.title: Tuts's current work and plans for a recording
segments.summary: Tuts says he is playing at a church, was laid off from the Gold Room on St. Charles, and is hunting a winter job; the researcher mentions a German interested in his music.

segments.title: Tuts on his reputation and trying the piano
segments.summary: Tuts mentions playing with Anderson and Captain John Handy, says he was among the greatest, and tries out the piano.

segments.title: Left hand, Gulf Coast job, Smiley Lewis, California, St. Louis, boogie-woogie
segments.summary: One very long block: Tuts on his strong left hand, Brother Montgomery and Dupree, his birth in 1907, the Isaiah Morgan band on the Gulf Coast, a trip to California in the 1940s, Smiley Lewis and his recordings, St. Louis, learning boogie-woogie from records, Wade Tait, and Red Cayou's real name.

segments.title: Adam Cato and little Butch revisited
segments.summary: Tuts repeats that Adam Cato went to Illinois, and that little Butch now teaches piano.
